Caroline (surname unknown) is a transgender woman; Melanie (surname unknown) is her friend and mutual supporter. They appreciate and encourage each other. Caroline moved from an unspecified home country about 2019; friends she had known four years by June 2023 supported her, especially after a difficult breakup. Family, friends, and mentors helped Caroline through transition and self-acceptance. Some friends did not accept her transition; her current relationships feel more genuine. Melanie says her husband and children motivate her; family is her greatest source of love and support.

Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group on May 7, 2023, and found trans stories inspiring and the group accepting; this gave her courage to embrace herself. She had been transitioning for three years by June 9. She advocates for LGBTQ inclusion: gave a school talk about her journey in the week before June 9, encouraging students to participate and be allies; their reactions were encouraging. She wants to use her voice to support trans people and promote understanding. She attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop June 23 and a pride parade during June 26–July 2, feeling welcomed and inspired. Attended an LGBTQ conference July 10 and a council adoption meeting July 14. Joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth July 15–16 and mentors a trans teen, helping build confidence; they attended a June pride event where Caroline was moved by the teen’s joy and community support. Joined Connected LGBTQ Activists July 18; group meets, plans campaigns/events, and supports members. Missed her city’s July 15–16 parade. Volunteered at an LGBTQ youth center by Aug 28, shared her story, found it emotional and fulfilling, and planned to continue; group prepared a children’s talent show for September. Attended a trans poetry reading Oct 6, finding it safe and empowering.

Caroline’s own experience of mental-health struggles and the support she received motivates interest in counseling/mental-health work, especially supporting trans people. She wants to offer a safe, welcoming space. She planned to attend a trans conference in July. Art has helped her explore gender, accept herself, and express hard-to-say feelings; she has made art since about age 17. Her painting about being a trans woman uses red/blue for binary gender and blended colors to reject rigid categories. Other works include “Embracing Identity” (acceptance, warmth, self-love), a tree and sun inspired by an LGBTQ center (unity/strength), stained glass about growth, potential, and togetherness, and a self-portrait with blue face (liberating, therapeutic). She enjoys flowers and nature subjects, abstract art, guitar (since about 2018), and piano; “Brave” by Sara Bareilles is meaningful. She planned an LGBTQ art show for August, later September, featuring LGBTQ artists to promote acceptance. A religious-conservative group upset her during a hike; supportive people reassured her. She enjoys blue, which calms her.

Caroline has long wanted to adopt and provide children a safe, loving home. By May 25, 2023, she was researching inclusive LGBTQ adoption agencies and intended to parent alone, hopeful but aware it would be hard. She sought friends’/mentors’ support. Applied to agencies the week before Aug 23 and was excited/nervous; got help from an adoption advice group. On Oct 13 contacted her mentor and felt ready. Passed agency interviews by Oct 20, a major step. Hopes to adopt children who have lacked a home and give them love, acceptance, and support. Advised Melanie Oct 13 to research agencies/lawyers and prepare references, finances, medical checks, and emotionally for a long wait.

Caroline’s grandmother in Sweden gave her a cross-and-heart necklace when she was young; it represents faith, love, roots, strength, and family. A friend made her a painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about 2013. Has guinea pig Oscar, especially fond of parsley. Rode horses with her father as a child. Enjoys reading; favorite book is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, which helped with hope, self-acceptance, and finding support. She is making a future children’s library with classics, multicultural stories, and educational books. Favorite childhood book unknown; Melanie’s is *Charlotte’s Web*.

Melanie is married (five years by June 2023, wedding circa 2018) and has children, including a youngest daughter and a son. Family outings and camping are especially meaningful. She enjoys beach trips (usually once or twice yearly), mountains, forest hikes, campfires, marshmallows, stories, and nature; family camped July 1–2, 2023, and in the mountains the week before June 27. In 2022 they watched the Perseids and made wishes. She remembers her youngest daughter’s first steps. Took children swimming (May 8), to a dinosaur museum (July 5), park (Aug 27), pottery workshop (July 14), and beach. Children enjoy nature and painting together; painted a palm-tree sunset July 8–9. On Aug 24 she volunteered with family at a homeless shelter, finding it hard but worthwhile. On Aug 13 celebrated her daughter’s birthday at a Matt Patterson concert. In October road trip, family visited Grand Canyon; son had an accident but was okay, frightening family and reminding Melanie to cherish them. Children were scared but reassured; she says they are resilient and give her strength. Trail outing Oct 19 helped her relax. Oct 21 bought two wooden doll figurines symbolizing family love.

Melanie values daily self-care: running, reading, clarinet (learned young), violin, and creativity; says caring for herself helps her family. Running farther by July 12 improved her mental health. She enjoys painting and pottery, about seven years by Sept 2023; pottery is therapeutic, expressive, calming, and important to her. Signed up for pottery July 2; made black-and-white flower bowl, colorful bowl, floral plate (Aug 24), and other work. September injury forced pottery break; by Oct 13 she was reading Caroline’s recommended book and painting. Paintings include lake sunrise (2022), horse on wooden wall, sunflower, pink-sky sunset, and abstract blue work; blue calms her. She likes landscape/still life and flowers, which recall joy and her wedding decor. Family loves painting together. Melanie plays clarinet and likes Bach, Mozart, and Ed Sheeran’s “Perfect.” Enjoys live music; saw band Summer Sounds playing upbeat pop. Pets include dog and cat Luna and Oliver (which name matches which unspecified); also mentioned Bailey and Oliver. Oliver hid a bone in her slipper; fed a carrot to a horse. Melanie shared a photo of black dog with frisbee. Melanie once shared photos of family scenes; pictured people are not necessarily identified. Caroline and Melanie attended a Pride festival together in 2022; planned a summer 2023 outing but completion unspecified.
